newsitem.title: USA: Discharged woman U.S. bomber pilot to appeal.
newsitem.headline: Discharged woman U.S. bomber pilot to appeal.

text.p: The first woman B-52 pilot will appeal the order under which she was allowed to resign from the U.S. Air Force to avoid being court-martialed for adultery and insubordination, her lawyer said on Sunday.

Lt. Kelly Flinn planned to file the appeal and seek an honourable discharge after Air Force Secretary Sheila Widnall, who decided her case, retires, perhaps later this year, lawyer Frank Spinner said on NBC's "Meet the Press."

Flinn in her first interview since accepting a general discharge from the Air Force told Time news magazine it was unfortunate the way the Air Force handled her case. She said she resigned rather than go to court-martial to save herself, her family and the Air Force from embarrassment.
"It's just not necessary for everybody to be out there to be reading these lurid details ... I'm the one who lived it and deep down in my heart I know what's true."

Flinn, 26 and single, earlier admitted having sex with Marc Zigo, a married civilian, but said he told her he had legally separated from his wife at the time of their affair. On Thursday she accepted a general discharge, avoiding a possible prison sentence if convicted.
In the Time interview she said she had hoped to be given an administrative disciplinary action that ranged from a reprimand to reduction in rank for her admitted mistakes.
"Then I could salute smartly, get Marc Zigo the hell out of my life and move on," she said.
Flinn said she would continue to keep flying "whether it's as an instructor, as a civilian or for a commercial airline."
Spinner predicted that Flinn might receive an honourable discharge from a new secretary, partly thanks to support she has received from some lawmakers.
Sen. Olympia Snowe, a Maine Republican who is the only woman on the Armed Services Committee, told "Meet the Press" she had hoped Flinn would get an honourable discharge from the Air Force.

Military officials described a general discharge as a separation from the Air Force with honour, but to a lesser degree than an honourable discharge. A general discharge is given when normally faithful service is marred by negative aspects of a person's duty performance or personal conduct.
In the Time interview Flinn asserted that Marc Zigo was to blame for her downfall.
She said within one week of meeting her, Zigo "told me he was in love with me and he would follow me anywhere."
"A feeling like this only comes around once in a lifetime, and you should seize it," she said.
Asked what lessons she learned from the whole incident, Flinn said laughing, "I think the next person I date is going to have to be fingerprinted and have a full background check."

Widnall in announcing on Thursday that Flinn was given a general discharge, said the pilot would leave the service in lieu of being court-martialed on charges she committed adultery, lied during an official investigation and disobeyed a direct order.
The discharge would prevent Flinn from flying for the Air Force Reserve or the Air National Guard unless she obtained a waiver, which Flinn's lawyer said she would seek.
But she will be able to fly civilian aircraft and her lawyer says she has already received phone calls of interest from some commercial airlines.
